algorithm.Title: Burns - Thermal - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Thermal burn/scald severity assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for airway/inhalation injury, electrical or chemical burn, major/deep/circumferential burn, face/neck/genital/hand/major-joint involvement, shock, or an unwell infant/child. Stop the burning source if safe, remove loose jewellery/clothing but not material stuck to skin, and cool a thermal burn with cool running water while preventing whole-body chilling. Brush off dry chemical first and follow 999 instructions. Do not use ice, creams, oils, or adhesive dressings. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Was the burn caused by an acid or another chemical rather than dry heat, hot liquid, or steam?
questions.Information: A chemical burn requires the authored Burns - Chemical pathway and immediate substance-specific decontamination precautions. Electrical exposure remains in the thermal-burn emergency rule-out rather than this redirect.

questions.Question: Is the burn very large or deep, on the face, genitals, or bottom, or was it caused by an acid, chemical, or electricity?
questions.Information: NHS.UK burns and scalds guidance lists large/deep burns, burns to the face/genitals/bottom, and chemical or electrical burns as emergency ambulance or Emergency Department criteria.

questions.Question: Is the caller unsure how serious the burn is, or is the patient a child under 5?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends seeking urgent clinical review whenever there is uncertainty about a burn or scald, and specifically for children under 5.

questions.Question: Is this a small, superficial burn or scald with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes small burns/scalds as manageable at home with first aid.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency burn response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive for airway/inhalation injury, electrical or chemical burn, major/deep/circumferential burn, face/neck/genital/hand/major-joint involvement, shock, or an unwell infant/child. Stop the burning source if safe, remove loose jewellery/clothing but not material stuck to skin, and cool a thermal burn with cool running water while preventing whole-body chilling. Brush off dry chemical first and follow 999 instructions. Do not use ice, creams, oils, or adhesive dressings. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: shock or reduced consciousness; increasing breathing difficulty or soot around airway; rapid swelling or circumferential burn.

advice.Title: Urgent burn review
Content: Cool the burn under cool running water for 15-30 minutes, cover loosely with cling film (not wrapped around the limb), and arrange same-day medical advice.
Call Back If: increasing pain or swelling; signs of infection.

advice.Title: Governed first aid for a clearly minor thermal burn
Content: Cool with cool running water, remove nearby loose jewellery/clothing before swelling but not anything stuck, prevent whole-body chilling, and cover loosely with a clean non-stick dressing. Do not burst blisters or apply ice, butter, toothpaste, creams, or adhesive material. Pain medicine requires age, weight, pregnancy, allergy, kidney/liver disease, and current-medicine checks.
Call Back If: increasing redness, pus, fever, swelling, or pain; blistering, deep/white/charred skin, or functional-area involvement.

references: NHS.UK, "Burns and scalds", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/burns-and-scalds/ (page last reviewed 31 March 2026)
